text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Please find attached the termination I received from the Erlenhof Cooperative.

I'm asking for help to be allowed to stay in my flat longer than the end of June date they have set. I know that date has now passed, but I simply couldn't leave. I am the only one who looks after my mother, who is 84, has dementia and lives three streets away; I go to her twice a day to give her her medication and meals. I also work nights at a bakery in Luzern. If I have to move out of town, I can't do either of those things, and in Luzern I haven't found anything I can afford at around CHF 1250 a month. I'm asking for a few more months, at least until the end of the year, so I can find something nearby and organise care for my mother.

The notice came by registered post and I signed for it on 21 April 2026, so I've had it in my hands since then.

I won't hide why it was sent. In February and March I couldn't pay the full rent because my hours were cut, and I ended up CHF 2365 behind. Mr Owen Zimmermann wrote to me in March giving me 30 days to pay the arrears and warned me that otherwise they would terminate the lease. I managed to pay only part of it in that time, and the termination says exactly that: it was given because I didn't pay what I owed within the deadline. My friend Ben Frei has since lent me the rest and the arrears are now cleared.

Thank you for any advice you can give me.

Anna Lehmann

Luzern, 20 April 2026

Termination of lease due to arrears

Dear Ms Lehmann,

By our letter of 13 March 2026 we set you a deadline of 30 days to pay outstanding rent of CHF 2365 and informed you that the lease would otherwise be terminated. As the amount was not paid in full within this deadline, we hereby terminate the lease for your flat at Dorfstrasse 108, Luzern, in writing with effect from 30 June 2026. The termination is given on the official form approved by the Canton of Lucerne, which is enclosed.

Yours sincerely,
Erlenhof Cooperative
Owen Zimmermann
